title: Longest Repeating Character Replacement
statement:
You are given a string `s` and an integer `k`. You can choose any character of the string and change it to any other uppercase English character, at most `k` times.

Return the length of the longest substring containing the same letter you can get after performing the above operations.

Slide a window and track the count of the most frequent character inside it. A window of length `windowLen` is achievable with at most `k` replacements when `windowLen - maxFreq <= k`; otherwise shrink from the left.
constraints: s consists of only uppercase English letters

examples.explanation: Replace the two 'A's or two 'B's to form "AAAA" or "BBBB".
Replace one 'A' in "AABA" to form "AABBA" -> "ABBB", giving a window of length 4.

editorial.approach: Use a sliding window with a frequency count of characters inside it. Track `maxFreq`, the count of the most frequent character seen in any window so far (it only needs to grow, never shrink, since a smaller window can't beat a previous best). At each step expand `right`, update counts and `maxFreq`. If the current window size minus `maxFreq` exceeds `k` (too many characters need replacing), shrink from `left`. The answer is the largest window size reached.
